text_blocks.snippet: Class 4 impact-resistant shingles are built to withstand severe hail and high winds—making them a smart upgrade for Utah homes along the Wasatch Front and hail-prone corridors.
snippet_highlighted_words: built to withstand severe hail and high winds

list.snippet: UL 2218 Standard: Underwriters Laboratories tests these materials by dropping a 2-inch steel ball from 20 feet onto the shingle twice in the same spot .
No Cracking: To earn a Class 4 rating, the shingle must endure the impact without cracking or fracturing on the underside.
SBS-Modified Asphalt: Many top Class 4 brands use rubberized (SBS-modified) asphalt, giving the shingle flexibility to absorb shock rather than snapping.

list.snippet: Insurance Discounts: Many insurance carriers operating in Utah offer annual homeowner policy discounts if you install a certified Class 4 roof (check with your specific provider before purchasing).

Lifespan & Weather Resistance: Typically designed to last around 20 to 30 years, handling Utah’s intense UV rays, freeze-thaw cycles, and summer thunderstorms better than standard 30-year composite shingles.
Note: Class 4 means impact-resistant, not indestructible; extreme storms or very large, jagged hail can still cause cosmetic or granule wear.
